The query runs in your browser with
[DuckDB-Wasm](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/wasm/overview), against `latest/`
attached as `bioc` (and selected with `USE bioc`, so `annotation.gene` works as
well as `bioc.annotation.gene`). The first run downloads DuckDB itself, a few
MB. One read-only `SELECT` or `WITH` at a time, capped at 1,000 rows.

Queries that filter and use `LIMIT` are fast, because DuckDB fetches only the
parts of each Parquet file it needs. Full scans of the big tables
(`raw.icite__metadata` is 12 GB, `annotation.icite__citation` 8 GB) are slow
and can run out of browser memory. For those, use DuckDB on your own machine.

### Queries to try

Copy one into the box, or open it in the DuckDB Shell.

```sql
-- Every table in the release, by schema
SELECT schema_name, view_name
FROM duckdb_views()
WHERE database_name = 'bioc' AND NOT internal
ORDER BY 1, 2;
```

```sql
-- Mouse genes by source
SELECT source, count(*) AS genes
FROM annotation.gene
WHERE taxon_id = 10090 AND valid_to IS NULL
GROUP BY source;
```

```sql
-- The provenance of this release
SELECT release, published_at, git_sha
FROM read_json('https://data.bioconice.cancerdatasci.org/latest/manifest.json');
```

```sql
-- One BugSigDB signature as a list of member names
SELECT bsdb_id, list(taxon_name ORDER BY member_index) AS members
FROM annotation.signature_taxon
WHERE bsdb_id = 'bsdb:83/1/1'
GROUP BY bsdb_id;
```
